settings.title: Settings
settings.language.help: Applies straight away — no restart. Map and creator names are never translated.
settings.minimizeToTray.help: Closing or minimizing the window keeps the app running in the system tray instead of quitting.
settings.hideFaqPopup.help: Stops the borderless-windowed reminder showing on startup.
settings.hideInMenu: Clear the map back in the menu
settings.hideInMenu.help: Only with Auto-detect map on: when the game returns to its main menu the match is over, so the overlay clears itself. The next Tab press detects the map again, even the same one.
settings.checkForUpdates.help: The only network request this app makes: one HTTPS call to GitHub Releases at startup to see whether a newer version exists. Turn it off to run fully offline. Map images are never downloaded — they ship inside the app.
settings.openLogFolder.help: If auto-detect misbehaves, open this folder and send detector.log — it records what the detector decided (map, score, timing), never any image.

settings.glide.help: 0 is the left/top edge of the screen, 100 the right/bottom edge.
settings.mapLabel.help: Shown at the bottom of the overlay, never rotated with the map, at the same opacity. The OBS window follows the same setting.
settings.waylandWarning: This session runs on Wayland, where dragging the overlay does not work. Use the fine-grain position sliders instead.
settings.placeByHand: To place the overlay by hand: show a map, press Set position, drag the overlay with the mouse, then press Stop setting position.
settings.setPositionWarning: Forgetting to stop setting position leaves the overlay catching your mouse clicks in game.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.fullscreen.q: The overlay does not show over the game
faq.fullscreen.a: Set Halloween: The Game to Borderless Windowed in its video settings. In exclusive fullscreen Windows gives the game exclusive control of the screen and no overlay window can draw on top of it.
faq.ban.q: Can the app get me banned?
faq.ban.a: It only displays image files that ship with it. It never reads the game's memory, never injects anything and never touches the game process in any way.
faq.screenshots.a: Only if you switch Auto-detect map on, and it is off by default. While it is on, the app captures the game's own window — not your screen, not any other window — about every 0.7 seconds while the game is running, and every 2 seconds while it is not, when there is no window to capture and nothing is captured. It compares that image, on your own computer, against small thumbnails of the in-game maps that ship inside the app. Nothing is saved to disk and nothing is uploaded: the only thing kept is which map it matched. Switch it off and nothing is captured at all.
faq.internet.a: Once, at startup: it asks GitHub whether a newer version of this app has been released, and nothing else. No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics. The map images are inside the app and are never downloaded. You can turn the check off under Settings → General → Check for updates on startup, after which the app makes no network requests at all.
faq.updates.a: When a newer version exists it is downloaded quietly in the background, and then a green banner appears at the top of this window. Nothing is installed until you press Restart and update there (or in the tray menu). The app then closes and a small window in the app's own colours takes its place, showing the steps and a progress bar; it works the disk for a few seconds, and then the app reopens by itself. The installer runs at low priority, so the rest of the PC stays responsive while it unpacks. If that window cannot start for any reason, the plain Windows installer runs instead — the update still happens. You are not asked anything and Windows does not prompt for permission — it installs only for your own user account. Press Later and the banner goes away for now; the update stays waiting for the next time you start the app. Closing or quitting the app never installs anything.
faq.updates.a2: If an update still drags, what is left is usually your antivirus reading every unpacked file. Adding %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Halloween Map Overlay to the exclusions under Windows Security → Virus & threat protection → Manage settings → Exclusions removes that cost.
faq.autodetect.a: Switch Auto-detect map on above the gallery, then press Tab in the game once at the start of a match. The overlay switches to that map and names it for a few seconds. It only switches when the map it sees is not the one already on the overlay, so a map you picked by hand is never replaced by itself — and it does follow the game again as soon as a different map comes up. Press Ctrl + Shift + D to clear the map and make it forget what it saw, so the next Tab press detects the same map again. When the game goes back to its main menu the overlay clears itself, whether auto-detect or you put that map there — but a map you pick while the menu is already on screen is left alone, so choosing the next map between matches is never undone. Turn that off under Settings → General.
faq.inTheWay.q: The overlay is in the way
faq.inTheWay.a: Press Ctrl + H to hide it, Ctrl + ↑ / ↓ to fade it, Ctrl + Shift + ↑ / ↓ to resize it, or move it under Settings → Overlay.
faq.obs.q: How do I record it in OBS?
faq.obs.a: Press Open OBS window, then capture that window in OBS and key out the green background with a chroma-key filter.
faq.customMaps.q: Can I add my own map images?
faq.customMaps.a: Yes — Add custom image in the menu. They appear in the gallery under the Custom creator.
